comparison.objective: Assemble a loose rack into a rack-and-pinion gripper at the correct tooth phase so both fingers open symmetrically; the candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper's opening stop.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1898 tests rack pickup, planar alignment, gear-tooth meshing, and symmetric jaw motion. The candidate tests coaxial driver seating, thin-jam-nut wrenching, and countertorque that preserves a screw setting.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1898 requires both racks seated, each jaw opened at least 15 mm, center error within 3 mm, and hands released for 1 s. The candidate requires a retained 90° opening within 3°, three repeat cycles, no more than 2° drift, retained nuts, and 30 mm clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparison.reason: Although both concern gripper mechanisms and verify motion after manipulation, gear-phase assembly is meaningfully different from preserving an adjustable stop while locking a concentric jam nut against reaction torque.

review_notes: Rack-pinion gripper assembly/even opening: compare ability, not gripper geometry.
